records.rationale: The real-world Claude Code pull-request study quantifies where agent-produced changes still require human revision and oversight.
This broad LLM-for-software-engineering review provides task and evaluation background without isolating multi-agent architectures.
This general review maps coding, testing, debugging, and accountability concerns but supplies no direct multi-agent comparison or concrete remedy.
This conceptual business-process manifesto does not study LLM multi-agent systems or software-development automation.
This systematic audit of 15 agent benchmarks uses software development as its primary case and directly exposes security, cost, and deployment-evaluation gaps.
This software-engineering research agenda maps dependability, transparency, and sustainability gaps without evaluating a multi-agent system or remedy.
This tutorial-like survey lists generic multi-agent topologies and sample implementations without controlled LLM or software-engineering evidence.
The experiments establish hallucination snowballing in sequential LLM collaboration and evaluate an entailment-based mitigation strategy.
The expert-validated judge comparison supplies transferable evidence on agreement, evaluator choice, and computational-cost tradeoffs for verification pipelines.
This empirical end-to-end test-generation study reports large model-dependent success and cost differences for a tool-using coding agent.
The system generates and scores educational assessments about software engineering rather than automating software development.
Triangle empirically validates specialized roles, negotiation, and automated mitigation for end-to-end incident triage in a real production cloud.
This nine-project study uses an LLM multi-agent system to parse microservice code and synthesize executable cross-service models with measured system gains.
AutoCodeRover demonstrates that structured code search and test-guided fault localization improve single-agent repair accuracy, speed, and cost.
The urban-diagnostics framework offers a transferable specialist-orchestration and handbook-grounded RAG design, although it remains theoretical and outside software engineering.
Controlled multi-agent experiments identify consensus-driven conformity and show that reasoning models mitigate it only for some task types.
This conceptual overview provides indirect background on delegation and socio-technical risk without a concrete software-engineering mechanism or evaluation.
AgileGen combines testable Gherkin requirements, iterative human decisions, and reusable scenario memory to align generated code with user intent.
This industry-academic vision maps reliability, accountability, security, and privacy challenges across the SDLC without evaluating a concrete control.
This documentation-and-modeling review supplies indirect task, dataset, prompting, and evaluation background but does not address multi-agent performance.
The evaluated IDE prototype uses branching, comparison, pruning, and provenance to make AI-generated code easier for humans to validate and govern.
The cross-domain comparison demonstrates standardized MCP tool orchestration, visible actions, and retained professional authority as transferable production controls.
The mediator-agent framework concretely unifies programmers, IDE tools, agentic tools, and external multi-agent systems across the SDLC, though it lacks evaluation.
This vehicular intrusion detector is a non-LLM multi-agent learning system outside software-development automation.
The cloud-automation study evaluates a single LLM agent under adversarial events and contributes transferable policy, identity, and remediation controls.
The controlled cross-domain study and ablations quantify gains from specialized generator, evaluator, optimizer, and advisor roles over individual models.
This software-compliance pipeline provides a concrete dual-agent and retrieval-grounded pattern for separating issue analysis from remediation guidance.
This low-substance editorial summarizes a broad software-engineering roadmap rather than presenting agentic evidence or a transferable method.
This construction-video recognition study is unrelated to LLM agents and software-development automation.
The evaluated staged workflow combines requirements analysis, shared context, retrieval, debugging, and user feedback to improve specialized code generation.
The one-question abstract about recommender agents provides no method, evidence, or transferable mechanism.
This conference-proceedings record is paired with an unrelated remote-work and parenting abstract and is a metadata collision.
This empirical-software-engineering vision identifies model and prompt drift as reproducibility threats requiring adapted instruments and validation standards.
The UML-to-timed-automata method uses UPPAAL model checking to preserve functional and nonfunctional consistency during autonomous software adaptation.
Yuma coordinates requirements-engineer and software-architect agents to produce deployable workflows with human validation at each step.
JsonATG empirically shows that specialized summarization and validation agents outperform two LLM test-generation methods and uncover confirmed library bugs.
